title: Latency During Privilege Escalation (sudo) and SSH Logins After Migration from SLES 15 SP7 to SLES 16 | SUSE | Support Center
plain_text:
Latency During Privilege Escalation (sudo) and SSH Logins After Migration from SLES 15 SP7 to SLES 16
Environment
Help Environment

SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 16 (Migrated from SLES 15 SP7)

Situation

After execution of OS migration from SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 SP7 to SLES 16, the system presents latency during privilege escalation via sudo -i and establishment of SSH sessions. The command prompt hangs before granting access.

The supportconfig logs show the following errors:

TLS negotiation failure in SSSD File: boot.txt and sssd.txt Log Snippet:

2026-03-06T11:55:26-03:00 lxl1pdisb015.dispositivos.bb.com.br sssd_be[1402]: Could not start TLS encryption. error:0A000410:SSL routines::ssl/tls alert handshake failure

systemd-logind failure due to Cgroups incompatibility File: boot.txt Log Snippet:

/proc/cgroups lists only v1 controllers, use cgroup.controllers of root cgroup for v2 info

D-Bus timeouts via PAM File: boot.txt Log Snippet:

sudo[735186]: pam_systemd(sudo-i:session): Failed to create session: Connection timed out

PAM module loading failures File: boot.txt Log Snippet:

sshd-session[689498]: PAM unable to dlopen(/usr/lib64/security/pam_cracklib.so): /usr/lib64/security/pam_cracklib.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

Resolution

Stabilizing the environment requires readjusting local cryptographic policies, removing constraints in the boot manager, and sanitizing authentication routines.

1. SSSD Cryptography and Timeout Configuration 

Edit the file /etc/sssd/sssd.conf. Locate the configuration block regarding the directory (e.g., [domain/LDAP.DESENVOLVIMENTO]) and add the fallback rules for cipher relaxation and TCP wait limits:

ldap_tls_cipher_suite = DEFAULT:@SECLEVEL=1
ldap_network_timeout = 3
ldap_opt_timeout = 3


Proceed to delete the cache database of the faulty domain and restart the daemon:

/usr/bin/rm -f /var/lib/sss/db/cache_*.ldb
/usr/bin/systemctl restart sssd.service


2. Cgroups v2

Edit the boot configuration /etc/default/grub. Identify the GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT variable and strictly remove the parameter: 

systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=0

Regenerate the boot matrix on the disk to apply the directive removal:

/usr/sbin/grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg


3. PAM

The PAM update replaces manual configurations with system defaults. Executing this process requires two concurrent SSH sessions to prevent lockout.

Session 1 (Control): Keep the current SSH connection logged in as root. Do not close this session. Open a second SSH terminal.

Session 1 (Backup): Create a backup of the PAM directory:

Back up the authentication configuration tree and use the native tool to purge links to discontinued libraries:

/usr/bin/cp -a /etc/pam.d /etc/pam.d.bkp

Session 1 (Update): Remove references to pam_cracklib.so and pam_lastlog.so:

/usr/sbin/pam-config -u


Note: If PAM files are centrally managed by automation engines (e.g., Puppet), manually remove the calls to pam_cracklib.so and pam_lastlog.so directly in the source templates; executing the pam-config utility will not be necessary.

Session 2 (Validation): Initiate a new SSH connection and test privilege escalation:

/usr/bin/sudo -i


Session 1 (Rollback - Upon Failure): If authentication fails in Session 2, revert the directory in Session 1:

/usr/bin/rm -rf /etc/pam.d && /usr/bin/mv /etc/pam.d.bkp /etc/pam.d


System Reboot

Reboot the server to load the GRUB profile and instantiate the D-Bus session daemons.

/usr/sbin/reboot
Cause

The latency and sequential collapse of authentications stem from the incompatibility of legacy configurations (from previous SLES versions) operating under the strict architectural and security policies of SLES 16.

SSSD TLS Version: SLES 16 utilizes the OpenSSL 3 library and elevates the default security level (SECLEVEL=2). The configured LDAP backend offers obsolete cipher algorithms or protocols, resulting in the immediate rejection of the TLS negotiation. The SSSD daemon synchronously exhausts the network layer timeout, causing the terminal to hang.

Cgroups v2: Recent branches of Systemd require the unified resource hierarchy (Cgroups v2) for management. The inherited compatibility parameter systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=0 in GRUB blocks the mapping of the new structure, forcing systemd-logind.service to fail during boot and preventing the allocation of new sessions by PAM.

PAM Libraries: The pam_cracklib and pam_lastlog modules have been discontinued from the OS base. The persistence of these calls in the static files under /etc/pam.d/ triggers repetitive runtime searches, degrading performance during the escalation process.

Additional Information
 Technical Differences Between SLE 15 and SUSE Linux 16:  https://documentation.suse.com/sles/16.0/html/SLE-differences-faq/

What is new in SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 16.0: https://www.openssl.org/docs/man3.0/man1/openssl-ciphers.html

Overview of OpenSSL versions in SUSE Linux Enterprise Server: https://support.scc.suse.com/s/kb/Overview-of-OpenSSL-versions-in-SUSE-Linux-Enterprise-Server-1583239464862?language=en_US
